subject: Grace-period and cross-border backup purge — alignment request
messages:
From: Claire Huang <claire.huang@medicohealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Dec 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Backup purge window + cross-border transfer question

Hi Vanessa,

Quick question as we finalize the DPA amendment — our security team wants to confirm the exact timing and mechanics for backup purges that may contain EU-sourced data. Specifically:

- What is Redwood's standard grace period after a deletion request before backups containing the record are purged?
- Are there any planned cross-border moves of older backups in the next 90 days that would affect EU residency?
- If we require a shorter window for retention in our region, what exception process / evidence will you need?

Attached is our current internal requirement doc for reference (no need to return it). We're hoping to lock timelines this week so LegalOps can draft the amendment.

Thanks — Claire
Claire Huang
Head of Security Programs
Medico Health

Attachment: medico-retention-needs.pdf (attachment stub)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Claire Huang <claire.huang@medicohealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Dec 2025 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Backup purge window + cross-border transfer question

Claire —

Thanks for the clear ask. High level answers below; I also attached a proposed purge timeline spreadsheet so we can align on specific datasets.

- Standard grace period: 30 days from the deletion confirmation for primary storage; backups containing deleted records are scheduled for purge in our weekly backup retention job 45–60 days after deletion (dependent on snapshot cadence).
- Cross-border moves: We have a scheduled one-time archival consolidation planned in early Jan 2026 to optimize cold storage costs. That consolidation is metadata-only for long-term archives and we can exclude EU-region snapshots for customers that require residency.
- Shorter window exceptions: We support contract-level retention carveouts. To approve an exception we need: 1) affected dataset identifiers, 2) justification and legal basis, 3) requested retention window, and 4) an authorized signatory on company letterhead.

Action items I propose:
1) I'll populate the attached sheet (backup_schedule_v1.xlsx) with our default timelines and the Jan consolidation dates.
2) Kimberly, can Legal confirm the exact wording Medico's amendment needs (DPA addendum vs clause)?
3) Claire, if you can flag any datasets that need residency carveouts in the sheet, we'll route the exception process.

I'll follow up after I get Kimberly's input.

— Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Trust & Privacy
Redwood Inference

Attachment: backup_schedule_v1.xlsx (attachment stub)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Claire Huang <claire.huang@medicohealth.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Dec 2025 13:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Backup purge window + cross-border transfer question

Vanessa / Claire —

Thanks for looping me in. For the DPA amendment, Legal generally prefers two approaches depending on client preference:

A) DPA addendum that enumerates retention windows and a carveout table per dataset (recommended for enterprise customers with many datasets).
B) Short clause added to the DPA that references an external schedule maintained by Redwood (recommended for smaller sets).

For Medico, given the residency ask, I'd recommend approach A. If we go that route we need the following from Medico to draft: dataset list + the exhibit with requested retention windows + signatory contact for execution.

Separately, we should produce a subprocessor inventory snapshot to attach as evidence for the transfer section. Karthik — can you export the current subproc list and include last-known data transfer locations? Please put in CSV and include any planned changes through Feb 2026.

I'll draft a short clause for the exception path and attach it here once ready.

Thanks,
Kimberly
Senior Counsel, Privacy
Redwood Inference

Attachment (coming): dpa_clause_suggestion.docx (attachment stub)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 12 Dec 2025 08:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Backup purge window + cross-border transfer question — subprocessor list

Kimberly / Vanessa / Claire —

Attached is the subprocessor snapshot and the short notes on which processors touch backups vs ephemeral logs (redwood_subprocessors_20251211.csv). Key points:
- Primary backup storage: CloudBucketCo (US, eu-central-1). We can apply regional-only buckets per contract.
- Cold archive consolidation (Jan 2026): will be executed by ArchiveOps (contracted subproc). We can opt-out for accounts requiring residency; opt-out requires the contract addendum to be signed before the consolidation job (planned 2026-01-05).
- Log retention exception: We currently retain operational logs for 180 days by default. We can mark Medico for a 30-day log retention exception as part of the DPA exhibit, but we need to confirm whether Medico needs any of those logs preserved for audit.

Claire — please confirm: 1) if you'd like Redwood to exclude EU backups from the Jan consolidation, and 2) whether the 30-day log retention would satisfy your compliance team. If Medico needs shorter than 30 days, provide the justification and we will route through legal/ops for feasibility.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Infrastructure Partnerships
Redwood Inference
